questions.title: Which club will sign Djed Spence on a permanent transfer from Tottenham Hotspur during summer 2026?
questions.background: Djed Spence is a Tottenham Hotspur player.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement from Tottenham Hotspur or the receiving club confirming a completed permanent transfer. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the club that signs Djed Spence directly from Tottenham Hotspur on a permanent transfer between June 1 and August 31, 2026. Loan agreements and unconfirmed transfer reports do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the receiving club.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-07 update (Sports Mole Aug 6-7, FCInterNews Aug 7, Football365/Liverpool Echo/Ben Jacobs/Sky Sports Mark McAdam Aug 7, TEAMtalk/Footy Hawk/Goal.com Aug 6): Major double breakdown of our prior top contenders forces a sharp flattening and higher residual. First, Sports Mole (Aug 6-7) reports Inter Milan walked away from advanced talks after balking at Spurs' GBP 35m (>EUR 40m) valuation, corroborated by FCInterNews (Aug 7) noting Spence is looking elsewhere in England — slashing Inter Milan 0.35 -> 0.12 (retaining partial weight only if Spurs compromise on price, as the sole club confirmed to have held formal talks earlier). Second, Liverpool are flatly ruled out by four independent sources on Aug 6-7: Liverpool Echo ('absolutely no intention'), Ben Jacobs ('not currently working on' him), Sky Sports' Mark McAdam (LFC will not sign a defender for 4-6 weeks), and FCInterNews — dropping Liverpool (0.13) out of our top 5. With Tom Barclay (The Sun) noting unnamed clubs hold stronger interest than Liverpool and Spence's camp offering him around for guaranteed starts, Manchester United take a modest #1 lead (0.14 -> 0.18; offered Spence as Lewis Hall alternative though not yet committed), ahead of Everton (0.11 -> 0.13; 7/1 odds and clear starting role), Inter Milan (0.12), Newcastle United (0.05 -> 0.10; cited monitoring Spence in TEAMtalk/Footy Hawk), and newly added AC Milan (0.07; named interested alongside Inter by Goal.com Aug 6, restrained by Serie A fee hurdle). Total sum lowered 0.78 -> 0.60, leaving 40% residual for unnamed PL/European suitors (e.g., Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace, Juventus, Chelsea).

local_articles.title: Michael Carrick being ‘careful’ with Mason Mount as Manchester United draw with PSG
local_articles.snippet: GOTHENBURG, Sweden - Michael Carrick said he had to be “careful” with Mason Mount after the England midfielder was involved in an injury scare during Manchester United’s 1-1 friendly draw with Paris Saint-Germain in Gothenburg on Aug 8. Mount, who joined United from Chelsea in 2023, has been hampered by injury problems since arriving at Old Trafford and he lasted less than 20 minutes after starting against PSG. The 27-year-old appeared to suffer a foot injury in Sweden and, following discussions with coaches on the touchline, left the field to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher. “He (Mount) got kicked,” United manager Carrick told reporters. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him. “We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.” Post-match video footage showed Mount walking on to the United bus without any form of visible knee support or a protective boot. questions.title: Which branch of Venezuela's government will the first government–opposition talks after Nicolás Maduro's removal agree to overhaul?
questions.background: Nicolás Maduro was removed from power in January 2026, and Delcy Rodríguez became acting president. Previous negotiations between Venezuela's government and opposition have not produced a lasting political settlement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from the negotiating parties or contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera. Resolution Conditions : Identify the branch of government that both sides agree to comprehensively overhaul during their first formal negotiating round following Maduro's January 2026 removal. The round must conclude by August 31, 2026. An announced agreement is sufficient; implementation is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The common name of the governmental branch, rather than an individual institution or officeholder.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-08-07 update (Infobae Aug 7, El Cooperante Aug 7, CNA Aug 7, CNN/CNN en Espanol Aug 6, local Reuters/Straits Times Aug 7): Day 1 of Caracas talks wrapped Aug 6 with methodology and a permanent session through Aug 12 ratified, confirming that the institutional overhaul agenda focuses exclusively on two branches: Electoral (CNE) and Judicial (TSJ). Two major Aug 7 revelations narrow the gap between them substantially: (1) Dinorah Figuera's explicit schedule puts TSJ reinstitutionalization FIRST (November 2026) ahead of CNE delivery (December 2026); and (2) Infobae reveals Jorge Rodriguez's National Assembly had already initiated a TSJ overhaul (passing a law reducing the Plenary Chamber from 32 to 20 magistrates) before pausing it specifically to move TSJ reform into this US-backed negotiation table. Electoral branch retains a modest lead (0.58 -> 0.50) as the talks' overarching transition goal toward elections and Chavismo's historical willingness to negotiate CNE composition first, while Judicial branch rises sharply (0.32 -> 0.42). Trimming Citizen (0.05 -> 0.04) and Legislative (0.03 -> 0.02) and holding Executive (0.02) keeps sum = 1.00 across Venezuela's five constitutional branches.

questions.title: Which country's mainland coastline will be confirmed contaminated by the Caroline Bezengi oil spill by August 13, 2026?
questions.background: The Caroline Bezengi has been leaking crude oil since running aground in June 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by government environmental authorities, or reliable news reports directly citing those statements. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the country whose mainland coastline is confirmed to have been contaminated by oil from the Caroline Bezengi by August 13, 2026. Offshore pollution, contamination confined to islands, and predictions of future landfall do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Decisive July 24-31 satellite and maritime confirmation (Reuters/Straits Times/gCaptain July 31, The Insider/Greenpeace July 31, Semafor July 28, The Week July 24): after an initial blast off Mukalla, Yemen on June 8, the sanctioned shadow-fleet Suezmax tanker Caroline Bezengi (IMO 9224439) drifted northeast and ran aground on June 12 on rocks off Jazirat Al-Qibliyyah in Oman's Al Hallaniyat Islands — roughly 45 km off Oman's mainland Dhofar/Al Wusta coast and >350 km northeast (downwind/downcurrent) of Yemen. Reuters verified the grounded vessel's identity from deck structures and paint, Greenpeace assessed 3-40 sq km of ongoing crude slicks, and July 28 satellite imagery shows a dark slick near the breached hull with lighter oil patches already spreading north of Al-Qibliyyah directly toward Oman's mainland coastline during peak July-August Southwest Monsoon winds/currents; Oman's Environment Authority issued oil-spill response guidance July 29 after Muscat's July 23 removal ultimatum went unanswered. Moving Oman sharply up (0.42 -> 0.85, capped at 0.85 pending official mainland-contamination confirmation under criteria), slashing Yemen (0.40 -> 0.08, retaining small residual for any delayed claim tied to the June 8 Mukalla blast), and placing small Arabian Sea / Gulf of Oman tails on Pakistan (0.02), Iran (0.02), and India (0.01) (sum 0.98).

questions.title: Which Israeli company will Save the Children Norway urge Norway's sovereign wealth fund to divest from by September 20, 2026?
questions.background: Norway's sovereign wealth fund reduced its holdings in Israeli companies in 2025, citing the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the Israeli company publicly identified by Save the Children Norway or its representatives as a divestment target over concerns that its products could contribute to violations of international humanitarian law. Use statements or contemporaneous reporting published between January 1 and September 20, 2026. Answer with the company's full name. Resolution Date : 2026-09-20 Accepted Answer Format : string (company)
questions.current_reasoning: Norway's NBIM reduced its Israeli holdings from 61 to 29 benchmark-listed firms in H2 2025, already divesting Bet Shemesh Engines and excluding five major Israeli banks (Bank Hapoalim, Bank Leumi, Mizrahi Tefahot, FIBI, FIBI Holdings) plus Caterpillar; Elbit Systems was excluded in 2009. Save the Children Norway's divestment target must be a remaining Israeli company whose products raise international humanitarian law concerns, putting defense-tech, chemical, and surveillance suppliers such as Next Vision Stabilized Systems (drone cameras), ICL Group, Cellebrite DI, Aryt Industries, and Gilat Satellite Networks at the top. Because ~29 Israeli holdings remain in NBIM's portfolio plus US-listed Israeli firms, substantial probability mass (0.58) is left unassigned across the wider field.

questions.title: Which country will the Spanish Football Federation announce as the host of the 2027 Spanish Super Cup?
questions.background: The Spanish Super Cup features the winners and runners-up of La Liga and the Copa del Rey. Saudi Arabia has hosted the competition since 2020.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Spanish Football Federation’s official host announcement, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country officially named as host of the 2027 Spanish Super Cup by August 31, 2026. This question concerns the announced host, not whether the tournament subsequently takes place there. Resolution occurs when the announcement is made. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the host country, rather than the host city or stadium.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-07 breaking report from Diario AS (David Aliaga & AS Director Jose Felix Diaz, 20:09 CEST): RFEF's Comision Delegada will meet next Thursday, August 13, 2026 to decide the host venue for the February 2027 Spanish Super Cup (Barcelona, Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid, Real Sociedad), and the shortlist has dramatically reshaped: (1) Miami (United States) is now explicitly reported as the #1 favorite ('Miami se posiciona como favorito'), lifting United States sharply 0.11 -> 0.45 — capped below 0.50 because the Comision Delegada has not yet voted, Louzan previously dropped Miami for the women's Supercopa after club pushback, and February transatlantic travel plus FIFA/CONCACAF approvals remain nontrivial hurdles. (2) Istanbul (Turkey) surges from outside top 5 into #2 at 0.29 ('Miami o Estambul, favoritas... con Estambul en segundo lugar'), offering UEFA jurisdiction (zero cross-confederation hurdles), minimal travel/time-zone shift before February UCL knockouts, and insulation from Gulf hostilities. (3) Qatar drops sharply 0.38 -> 0.14 after AS explicitly downgraded Doha to the third option ('parte con menos opciones... tercera via'), reinforced by ongoing Iran-war Gulf security risks (Straits Times Aug 6 notes F1 reviewing its Nov/Dec Qatar and Abu Dhabi races). (4) Spain (0.13 -> 0.045, domestic fallback if foreign negotiations stall) and Mexico (0.16 -> 0.035, absent from AS's Aug 7 top-3 shortlist) retain modest tail probabilities, with Egypt exiting top 5 (~0.015). Top-5 sum = 0.96, leaving 0.04 outside for Egypt, UAE, China, Morocco, Saudi Arabia, and other.

questions.title: Who will score Bangladesh's first men's Test century on Australian soil?
questions.background: A Test century is an individual score of at least 100 runs in a single innings. No Bangladesh batter has yet achieved this milestone in a men's Test played in Australia.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official Test match scorecards and contemporaneous reputable cricket reporting confirming the first such century. Resolution Condition : The question resolves when a player representing Bangladesh first reaches 100 runs in a single innings of an official men's Test match played in Australia. Accepted Answer Format : The batter's full name.
